examples.en: Scientists explore the deep sea.
The research team surveyed a big cave yesterday.
Our country will explore Mars soon, too.
A ship to survey the new island has set out.
I explored the mountains and wrote a report.

examples.ko: 로봇이 위험한 곳을 대신 탐사해서 안전해요.
examples.en: A robot explores the dangerous place instead, so it is safe.

explain: 탐사하다는 바다, 우주, 땅속처럼 잘 모르는 곳을 직접 가서 살필 때 써요. '우주 탐사', '해저 탐사'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요. 사건이나 사람을 알아볼 때는 '조사하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 탐사하다 is for going to a place you do not know well, like the sea, space or underground, and examining it yourself. It also appears as a noun: '우주 탐사' (space exploration). For looking into an incident or a person, use '조사하다'.

examples.en: The police crack down on illegal parking.

examples.ko: 어제 시청에서 쓰레기 무단 투기를 단속했어요.
examples.en: City hall cracked down on illegal dumping yesterday.

examples.ko: 다음 달부터 속도 위반을 더 강하게 단속할 거예요.
examples.en: From next month they will enforce speeding rules more strictly.

examples.ko: 단속하는 직원이 오자 사람들이 자리를 옮겼어요.
examples.en: When the enforcement officer came, people moved away.
They are cracking down on speeding, so the road is jammed.
After the street stalls were cracked down on, the market became quiet.

explain: 단속하다는 규칙을 어기는 사람을 잡고 막는 일이라서 경찰이나 시청 같은 기관이 주어일 때가 많아요. '불법 주차 단속', '단속 기간'처럼 명사로도 써요. '입단속'처럼 말을 조심하게 하는 뜻도 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 비밀이 새지 않게 말을 조심하라고 미리 못 박을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you warn people in advance to keep a secret.

explain_en: 단속하다 is about catching and stopping people who break rules, so the subject is often an organization such as the police or city hall. It is also used as a noun: '불법 주차 단속' (illegal parking enforcement). '입단속' means making sure someone keeps quiet.

examples.en: When it rained, even the dry land became moist.
Farmers grow grain on the wide land.

examples.ko: 이 집은 대지는 넓은데 건물은 작아요.
examples.en: This house has a large lot, but the building is small.
When spring comes, sprouts come up from the ground.
The children ran freely across the wide land.
An earthquake struck and the ground shook hard.

explain: 대지는 넓게 펼쳐진 땅을 글 같은 느낌으로 부르는 말이라서 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 보통 '땅'이라고 해요. 건물을 짓는 땅은 '대지 면적'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 대지 is a literary way to call wide stretches of land, so you see it in news and writing. In everyday speech people usually say '땅'. For a plot of land for a building, it appears as in '대지 면적' (lot area).

examples.en: Would it be rude to call this late?
Wouldn't it be impolite to take photos here?
Speaking casually to an elder is rude.

examples.ko: 제가 한 말이 실례된 것 같아서 죄송해요.
examples.en: I am sorry; what I said seems to have been rude.

examples.ko: 식사 중에 전화를 받는 건 실례되는 행동이에요.
examples.en: Answering the phone during a meal is rude behavior.
If it was rude to the guest, I apologize.

explain: 실례되다는 상대에게 예의가 없게 느껴지는 일에 써요. '실례가 되다'로 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요. 내가 한 행동을 사과할 때는 '실례했어요'를 써요.
explain_en: 실례되다 is for things that would feel impolite to the other person; you can also say it in two words, '실례가 되다'. When apologizing for something you did, use '실례했어요'.

examples.en: The bus is delayed because of an accident.
The delivery was delayed because the construction ran long.
Please tell me in advance if the schedule is delayed.

examples.ko: 눈 때문에 비행기 출발이 지체될 것 같아요.
examples.en: The flight departure seems likely to be delayed because of snow.
The delay was long, so I waited a lot.

examples.ko: 서류가 늦게 와서 일이 지체돼서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: The documents came late and the work is delayed, so I am worried.

explain: 지체되다는 있어야 할 시간보다 늦어질 때 써요. 주어는 일정, 배송, 교통처럼 일의 진행이에요. 사람이 약속에 늦는 건 '늦다'나 '지각하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 지체되다 is for things that run later than they should; the subject is a schedule, delivery, traffic or other process. For a person being late to an appointment, use '늦다' or '지각하다'.

examples.en: I play chess with a friend every weekend.
Chess has rules that are a bit difficult.
I learned how to play chess from my father.
My younger sibling won a prize at a chess tournament.
My hobbies are chess and reading.
The pieces disappeared from the chessboard one by one.

explain: 체스는 '두다'와 같이 써요. '체스를 두다'처럼 말해요. 바둑이나 장기도 '두다'를 쓰고, 카드 게임은 '치다'를 써요.
explain_en: Chess goes with the verb '두다': '체스를 두다'. Go (바둑) and Korean chess (장기) also use '두다', while card games use '치다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays on the school hockey team.
I joined a club because I wanted to learn hockey.
I went to the field to watch a hockey game.
The hockey players practice hard every day.
I like soccer more than hockey.
I bought a new hockey stick.

explain: '하키'라고만 하면 보통 필드하키를 말하고, 얼음 위에서 하는 건 '아이스하키'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: Plain '하키' usually means field hockey; the version played on ice is called '아이스하키'.

examples.en: I majored in physics at university.
The physics exam is tomorrow, so I am worried.
Physics is hard but fun.
That professor is famous in the field of physics.
My younger sibling wants to go to the physics department.
I borrowed a physics book from the library.

explain: 물리학, 화학, 수학처럼 '-학'으로 끝나는 말은 공부하는 분야 이름이에요. 물리학을 연구하는 사람은 '물리학자', 대학의 학과는 '물리학과'예요. 보통 '물리학을 전공하다', '물리학을 공부하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Words ending in '-학' such as 물리학, 화학 and 수학 are names of fields of study. A person who researches physics is a '물리학자', and the university department is '물리학과'. It is usually used as in '물리학을 전공하다' or '물리학을 공부하다'.

examples.en: The ID card is issued within a week.
The passport was issued yesterday.
I will send you a text once the document is issued.
You have to wait until the card is issued.

examples.ko: 발급되는 데 보통 삼 일쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It usually takes about three days to be issued.
The certificate was issued wrongly, so I applied again.

explain: 발급되다는 증명서, 여권, 카드처럼 관청이나 회사가 만들어 주는 서류에 써요. 주어는 서류예요. 서류를 만들어 주는 쪽은 '발급하다', 받는 쪽은 '발급받다'를 써요.
explain_en: 발급되다 is for documents that an office or company produces, such as certificates, passports and cards; the subject is the document. The issuing side uses '발급하다' and the receiving side uses '발급받다'.

examples.en: The district office issues residence certificates.
The bank issued a new card.
The school will issue a graduation certificate.

examples.ko: 서류를 발급하는 창구는 이 층에 있어요.
examples.en: The counter that issues documents is on the second floor.

examples.ko: 직원이 증명서를 발급하고 나서 제게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: After the staff issued the certificate, they explained it to me.
The staff issued a receipt and gave it to me.

explain: 발급하다는 주는 쪽인 구청, 은행, 학교가 주어예요. 받는 쪽은 '발급받다'를 써요. 그래서 '구청이 여권을 발급했어요'와 '여권을 발급받았어요'가 둘 다 맞아요.
explain_en: The subject of 발급하다 is the issuing side, such as a district office, bank or school. The receiving side uses '발급받다', so both '구청이 여권을 발급했어요' and '여권을 발급받았어요' are correct.

examples.en: The police sealed off the accident scene.
It snowed a lot, so they close off the mountain road.
The government may seal the border.
They sealed off the entrance and evacuated people.

examples.ko: 도로를 봉쇄하는 바람에 차가 못 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Because the road was blocked off, cars could not pass.

examples.ko: 병원이 건물을 봉쇄해서 아무도 못 들어가요.
examples.en: The hospital sealed the building, so no one can enter.

explain: 봉쇄하다는 길, 문, 국경을 막아서 드나들지 못하게 할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '도로 봉쇄', '국경 봉쇄'처럼 자주 보여요. 그냥 문을 닫는 건 '닫다', 길을 막는 건 '막다'를 써요.
explain_en: 봉쇄하다 is for blocking roads, doors or borders so nobody can get in or out. News often shows '도로 봉쇄' and '국경 봉쇄'. Simply closing a door is '닫다' and blocking a road is '막다'.

examples.en: That actress acts really well.
I wanted to become an actress since I was little.
I met a famous actress at the film festival.

examples.ko: 새 영화의 주인공은 신인 여배우로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: A newcomer actress was chosen as the lead of the new movie.
I read that actress's interview in a magazine.
I want to take a photo with that actress.

explain: 여배우는 여자 배우를 가리켜요. 요즘은 성별 없이 그냥 '배우'라고 하는 경우도 많아요. 반대로 남자 배우는 '남자 배우'라고 풀어서 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: 여배우 means a female actor. Nowadays many people just say '배우' without mentioning gender. For male actors people often say it in two words, '남자 배우'.

en: get off; step down (from a show)

examples.en: I get off at the next stop.
After getting off the subway, I got lost.
To get off the bus, you have to press the bell.

examples.ko: 하차하는 승객이 다 내린 뒤에 타세요.
examples.en: Please board after the passengers getting off have all left.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 건강 문제로 드라마에서 하차했어요.
examples.en: That actor left the drama because of health problems.
My friend got off at the station and took a taxi.

explain: 하차하다는 안내 방송이나 공지에서 자주 들리는 말이고, 평소에 말할 때는 보통 '내리다'를 써요. 반대말은 '승차하다'예요. 방송 프로그램에서 빠지는 것도 '하차'라고 해요.
explain_en: 하차하다 is often heard in announcements and notices; in daily speech people usually say '내리다'. The opposite is '승차하다'. Leaving a TV program is also called '하차'.

examples.en: I watched this cartoon with Korean dubbing.
The dubbing felt awkward, so I watched it again with subtitles.
A famous voice actor took on the dubbing of the main character.
Children like dubbed movies.
Is there an English dubbed version, too?
I played a movie dubbing game with my friend.

explain: 더빙은 목소리를 다른 말로 바꿔 넣는 것이고, 자막은 글자로 보여 주는 거예요. 그래서 '더빙으로 보다', '자막으로 보다'처럼 나눠서 말해요. 더빙을 하는 사람은 '성우'라고 불러요.
explain_en: Dubbing replaces the voices, while subtitles show the words as text. So people say '더빙으로 보다' or '자막으로 보다'. People who do the voices are called '성우' (voice actors).

examples.en: I bought a new domain for my website.
The shorter a domain name is, the easier it is to remember.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 도메인이 아직 사용 가능한지 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked whether our shop's domain is still available.
I send emails from the company domain.

examples.ko: 도메인 주소가 바뀌어서 접속이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The domain address changed, so I cannot connect.

examples.ko: 이 도메인은 이미 다른 사람이 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: Someone else is already using this domain.

explain: 도메인은 '사다', '등록하다'와 자주 같이 써요. 영어 domain을 그대로 읽은 외래어예요. 인터넷 주소 전체는 '주소'라고 해요.
explain_en: 도메인 often goes with '사다' and '등록하다'. It is the English word domain read in Korean. The whole web address is just called '주소'.

examples.en: What is the hourly wage at this shop?
I asked the boss to raise my hourly wage.

examples.ko: 시급은 낮지만 일이 편해서 계속 다녀요.
examples.en: The hourly wage is low, but the work is easy, so I keep going.

examples.ko: 시급으로 받으면 일한 시간만큼 돈이 나와요.
examples.en: If you are paid hourly, you get money for the hours you work.

examples.ko: 새로 일하는 곳은 시급 외에 식사도 줘요.
examples.en: My new workplace gives meals in addition to the hourly wage.
The work is too hard for the hourly wage.

explain: 시급은 한 시간 일하면 받는 돈이고, 월급은 한 달 일하고 받는 돈이에요. 아르바이트는 보통 시급으로 말해요. '시급이 높다', '시급을 올리다'처럼 써요. '시급하다'는 급하다는 뜻의 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: 시급 is the pay for one hour of work, and 월급 is the pay for a month. Part-time jobs are usually described by 시급. It goes with '시급이 높다' and '시급을 올리다'. '시급하다' is a different word meaning urgent.

examples.en: How can your voice be this pretty?
Maybe it will rain tomorrow.
How are you so good at cooking?
Perhaps he has arrived by now.

examples.ko: 어쩜 말도 없이 그냥 가 버렸어요?
examples.en: How could he just leave without a word?

examples.ko: 어쩜 제 생각이 틀릴 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Maybe my thinking could be wrong.

explain: 어쩜은 '어쩌면'의 줄임말처럼 쓰여서 '아마 그럴지도 몰라요'라는 느낌을 줘요. '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'처럼 놀라거나 감탄할 때도 써요. 이때는 뒤에 '이렇게', '그렇게'가 자주 와요.
explain_en: 어쩜 works as a short form of '어쩌면' and gives the feeling of 'perhaps'. It is also used to express surprise or admiration, as in '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'. In that use, '이렇게' or '그렇게' often follows.

examples.en: The concert tickets have already been booked.
Train tickets can be booked from a month ahead.
A text arrives once the ticket is booked.

examples.ko: 좌석이 예매되는 데 몇 초밖에 안 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took only a few seconds for the seats to be booked.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 영화는 빨리 예매돼서 표를 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Popular movies get booked fast, so tickets are hard to get.
Can a booked ticket be canceled?

explain: 표를 미리 사는 사람은 '예매하다'를 쓰고, 표가 미리 팔린 상태는 '예매되다'로 말해요. '표를 예매했어요'와 '표가 예매됐어요'처럼 주어가 달라요. '매진되다'는 표가 다 팔렸다는 뜻이라 달라요.
explain_en: The person buying a ticket in advance uses '예매하다', and the ticket's state is described with '예매되다': '표를 예매했어요' versus '표가 예매됐어요'. '매진되다' is different; it means the tickets are sold out.

examples.en: My older brother enlists next month.
He enlisted right when he turned twenty.
That singer is scheduled to enlist next year.
On the day he enlisted, the whole family saw him off.

examples.ko: 친구는 대학교를 마치고 입대해서 이 년 뒤에 돌아와요.
examples.en: My friend enlisted after finishing university and returns in two years.
Before enlisting, I traveled with friends.

explain: 입대하다는 군대에 들어갈 때 쓰고, 군대에서 나올 때는 '제대하다'를 써요. 한국에서는 남자들이 보통 군대에 가야 해서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: 입대하다 is for entering the military, and leaving it is '제대하다'. In Korea men are generally required to serve, so this word comes up often.

examples.ko: 아침 아홉 시에 학교 앞에 집합해요.
examples.en: We assemble in front of the school at nine in the morning.
The students assembled on the field.
We will meet up in front of the station tomorrow.
The place to assemble is in front of the main gate.
After everyone gathered, we left together.
We gathered on time and boarded the bus.

explain: 집합하다는 정해진 시간에 정해진 장소로 모이는 일에 써서 선생님이나 팀장이 지시하는 느낌이 있어요. 친구끼리 약속할 때는 '모이다', '만나다'를 써요. '집합!'은 모이라는 구령으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: 집합하다 is for gathering at a set time and place, and it feels like an instruction from a teacher or team leader. Friends making plans use '모이다' or '만나다'. '집합!' is also used as an order to gather.

examples.en: Communication is the most important thing in a team.

examples.ko: 대화가 적어서 팀 커뮤니케이션을 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: We talk little, so we decided to increase team communication.
They hire people with good communication skills.
I take a communication class.
Foreign languages are a big help for communication.
People communicate not only with words but also with facial expressions.

explain: 커뮤니케이션은 회사나 학교 이야기에 자주 나오는 외래어이고, 같은 뜻으로 '소통'도 써요. '커뮤니케이션을 하다', '커뮤니케이션이 되다', '커뮤니케이션이 잘 안 되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 커뮤니케이션 is a loanword that often appears in talk about work or school, and '소통' can be used for the same idea. Typical uses are '커뮤니케이션을 하다', '커뮤니케이션이 되다' and '커뮤니케이션이 잘 안 되다'.

examples.ko: 마당에 오래된 펌프 한 대가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old pump in the yard.
I pumped the water up with a pump.

examples.ko: 자전거 바퀴에 바람을 넣으려고 펌프를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pump to put air in the bicycle tire.

examples.ko: 펌프가 고장 나서 물이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The pump is broken, so no water comes out.
A pump can also be operated by hand.
A strange noise comes from this pump.

explain: 물에는 '물 펌프', 자전거에는 '공기 펌프'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서 구분해요. 펌프를 움직이는 일은 '펌프질'이라고 하고, '펌프질하다'로 써요.
explain_en: You add a word in front to tell kinds apart, like '물 펌프' (water pump) and '공기 펌프' (air pump). Operating a pump is '펌프질', used as '펌프질하다'.

examples.ko: 자동차 딜러가 차 종류를 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The car dealer explained the types of cars.
I met a dealer because I wanted to buy a new car.
I asked the dealer to lower the price.

examples.ko: 외환 딜러는 하루 종일 화면을 봐요.
examples.en: A foreign exchange dealer watches the screen all day.
I signed the car contract after talking with the dealer.
I have a friend who works as a dealer.

explain: 딜러는 앞에 말을 붙여서 어떤 일을 하는지 말해요. '자동차 딜러', '외환 딜러'처럼요. 물건이 아니라 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
explain_en: 딜러 takes a word in front to say what the person deals in, as in '자동차 딜러' and '외환 딜러'. It refers to a person, not a thing.

examples.en: I bought a new mouse pad.
It is a jacket with pads in the shoulders.
I put on knee pads, too, and went skating.
This pad is soft, so it is comfortable to sit on.
Thanks to the pad, the chair is soft.
Water got on the pad, so I wiped it.

explain: 패드는 부드럽게 대거나 받치는 물건에 두루 쓰이는 외래어예요. '마우스 패드', '무릎 패드'처럼 앞말이 무엇인지 알려 줘요. 겨울에 입는 두꺼운 옷은 '패딩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 패드 is a loanword for soft things placed against or under something. The word in front tells you which kind, as in '마우스 패드' and '무릎 패드'. The thick padded winter jacket is called '패딩'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a fencer.
I watched a fencing match at the Olympics.
In fencing, quick footwork is important.
I am learning fencing at school.
The Korean fencing team won a gold medal.

examples.ko: 펜싱 마스크를 쓰면 얼굴이 안 보여요.
examples.en: When you wear a fencing mask, your face is not visible.

explain: 펜싱은 칼로 점수를 겨루는 운동이에요. 에페, 플뢰레, 사브르 세 종목이 있어요. '펜싱을 하다'처럼 말하고, 탁구나 테니스는 '치다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Fencing is a sport where two people score points with swords. There are three events: epee, foil and sabre. You say '펜싱을 하다', while table tennis and tennis sometimes take '치다'.

en: by any chance; if by some chance

examples.ko: 혹 길을 잃으면 이 번호로 전화하세요.
examples.en: If you happen to get lost, call this number.

examples.ko: 혹 제가 잘못 들었다면 다시 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If I happened to hear it wrong, please say it again.

examples.ko: 혹 내일 시간이 되면 같이 가요.
examples.en: If you happen to have time tomorrow, let's go together.
If I happen to be late, please start first.
If it should rain, take an umbrella.

examples.ko: 혹 질문이 있으면 편하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you happen to have a question, feel free to ask.

explain: '혹시'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 글 같은 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '혹시'를 써요. '혹'은 '혹 ~(으)면'처럼 조건 앞에 오고, '혹은'(=또는)은 다른 말이에요. 몸에 난 '혹'도 소리만 같은 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: It means about the same as '혹시' but sounds more bookish; in everyday conversation people usually say '혹시'. '혹' comes before a condition, as in '혹 ~(으)면', and '혹은' (meaning 'or') is a different word. The lump on the body, '혹', only sounds the same.

examples.ko: 제가 간단한 마술을 하나 보여 줄게요.
examples.en: I will show you a simple magic trick.

examples.ko: 아이들이 마술 쇼를 보고 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The children watched the magic show and clapped.
My uncle is very interested in magic.
Something like magic happened.
Magic is a trick, but it is amazing to watch.
I am curious about the secret of that trick.

explain: 마술은 속임수로 신기하게 보여 주는 공연이고, '마법'은 이야기 속의 진짜 힘이에요. 그래서 쇼에서는 '마술', 동화나 게임에서는 '마법'을 써요.
explain_en: 마술 is a performance that amazes with tricks, while '마법' is real power in a story. So shows use '마술', and fairy tales or games use '마법'.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 일 년 사이클로 제품을 새로 내요.
examples.en: This company releases new products on a one-year cycle.
The cycle of new products coming out keeps getting shorter.

examples.ko: 동생은 사이클 선수가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a cycling athlete.
When the wash cycle ends, the washing machine stops.
The moon's cycle is about a month.
On weekends I go cycling along the Han River.

explain: '사이클'과 '주기'는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 경우가 많아요. '생활 사이클', '제품 사이클'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여요. 자전거 경기를 가리킬 때도 쓰는데, 자전거 타기는 보통 '자전거를 타다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: '사이클' and '주기' can often replace each other. A word goes in front, as in '생활 사이클' and '제품 사이클'. It can also mean the cycling sport, but riding a bike is usually said '자전거를 타다'.

examples.en: In games, control is important.
Your mouse control gets better with practice.
A pitcher needs good control.
I hold the Control key and copy the text.
I was not confident in my control, so I drove slowly.
Control is also hard when the car slips.

explain: '컨트롤이 좋다', '컨트롤이 안 되다'처럼 잘 다루는 정도를 말해요. 야구에서 투수가 공을 원하는 곳에 던지는 능력은 '제구력'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: 컨트롤 describes how well you handle something, as in '컨트롤이 좋다' and '컨트롤이 안 되다'. In baseball, a pitcher's ability to throw where he wants is also called '제구력'.

examples.en: Even when I am angry, I control my emotions.
The pitcher controlled the ball well.
I will manage my weight for my health.
I learned how to control the robot.
I controlled my speed and came down slowly.
The child controlled himself and did not cry.

explain: '감정을 컨트롤하다', '체중을 컨트롤하다'처럼 목적어를 앞에 두고 써요. 속도나 온도를 맞출 때는 '조절하다', 기계를 움직일 때는 '조종하다'가 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It takes an object, as in '감정을 컨트롤하다' and '체중을 컨트롤하다'. For adjusting speed or temperature, '조절하다' is often more natural, and for operating a machine, '조종하다'.

examples.en: The players ran out onto the field.
Children kick a ball on the field.
It rained, so the field got wet.
The field was full of players.

examples.ko: 은퇴하는 선수가 그라운드를 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: The retiring player made one lap around the field.
Fans are happy when the team wins on its home ground.

explain: 학교의 넓은 마당은 '운동장'이라고 하고, 그라운드는 야구나 축구 경기 기사에서 자주 보여요. 자기 팀이 쓰는 경기장은 '홈 그라운드'라고 해요.
explain_en: A school's wide yard is a '운동장', while 그라운드 often appears in reports about baseball or soccer games. A team's own stadium is its '홈 그라운드'.

examples.en: A ship checks its surroundings with radar.
A strange object showed up on the radar.

examples.ko: 공항 옆에 큰 레이더 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A large radar stands next to the airport.
Radar can also find rain clouds.

examples.ko: 레이더가 고장 나서 비행기가 늦게 떴어요.
examples.en: The radar broke, so the plane took off late.
Work to install a new radar has begun.

explain: '레이더에 잡히다'처럼 무언가가 발견될 때 말해요. 날씨 뉴스에서는 '기상 레이더'가 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in '레이더에 잡히다' when something is detected. Weather news mentions '기상 레이더' (weather radar).

examples.en: We ate lunch boxes on the park lawn.
After even mowing the yard lawn, I am tired.
Lawn grass grows fast in summer.
You must not walk on the grass.
It rained, so the grass grew green.
They laid new turf on the soccer field.

explain: 잔디는 '잔디를 깎다', '잔디를 심다'처럼 써요. 길가에 저절로 나는 '풀'과 달리 곱게 가꾸는 풀이에요. 잔디가 깔린 넓은 곳은 '잔디밭'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 잔디 is used as in '잔디를 깎다' (mow the lawn) and '잔디를 심다' (plant grass). Unlike '풀' that grows by itself along the road, it is grass that is tended. A wide area covered with it is a '잔디밭'.

examples.en: My older brother finally got a job at a big company.
If you prepare hard, you will surely get hired.
My older sister got a job in Seoul and moved.
I counted the days until I would get a job.

examples.ko: 병원에 취직되면 월급을 모아서 여행을 갈래요.
examples.en: If I get hired at the hospital, I will save my pay and travel.

examples.ko: 아는 선배가 취직된 회사에 저도 지원했어요.
examples.en: I also applied to the company where a senior I know got hired.

explain: 취직하다는 내가 일자리를 얻는 행동이고, 취직되다는 합격해서 일하게 된 결과에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 구직 과정은 '취직을 준비하다', 결과는 '취직이 됐다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 취직하다 is the act of getting a job yourself, while 취직되다 focuses on the result of being accepted and starting work. So the process is '취직을 준비하다' and the result is '취직이 됐다'.

examples.en: The uncle got his nephew a job at his company.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아들을 빨리 취직시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The parents want to get their son a job quickly.

examples.ko: 선배가 저를 아는 회사에 취직시켜 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior got me a job at a company he knows.
The father tried hard to get his daughter a job at a bank.
I thanked the boss who gave my friend a job.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 취직시킬 방법이 없어서 고민이에요.
examples.en: I am worried because there is no way to get that person a job.

explain: 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다'처럼 일하게 해 주는 사람과 일자리를 얻는 사람이 따로 있어요. 내가 일자리를 얻는 건 '취직하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다', the person who arranges the job and the person who gets it are different. When you get a job yourself, use '취직하다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays the drums in a band.

examples.ko: 드럼 소리가 너무 커서 이웃이 항의했어요.
examples.en: The drum sound was so loud that a neighbor complained.
I attend a drum academy.
This song starts with the drums.
The drums play a big role in keeping rhythm.

examples.ko: 드럼 스틱을 두 개 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two new drumsticks.

explain: 드럼은 '드럼을 치다'처럼 '치다'와 같이 써요. 연주하는 사람은 '드러머'예요. 바이올린은 '켜다', 플루트는 '불다'를 써서 악기마다 동사가 달라요.
explain_en: Drums go with '치다': '드럼을 치다'. A person who plays drums is a '드러머'. Each instrument takes its own verb: the violin uses '켜다' and the flute uses '불다'.

examples.en: They made the floor of the building from concrete.
We waited a day for the concrete to harden.
There are many concrete buildings in the city.

examples.ko: 콘크리트 길은 비가 와도 흙탕물이 안 생겨요.
examples.en: A concrete road does not get muddy water even when it rains.
Workers poured concrete and built a wall.

examples.ko: 차가운 콘크리트 위에 앉으면 엉덩이가 시려요.
examples.en: If you sit on cold concrete, your bottom gets chilly.

explain: '콘크리트를 붓다', '콘크리트가 굳다'처럼 써요. '시멘트'는 콘크리트를 만드는 가루 재료라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as in '콘크리트를 붓다' (pour concrete) and '콘크리트가 굳다' (concrete hardens). '시멘트' is the powder used to make concrete, so the two are different.

examples.en: At the zoo, the hippo opened its mouth wide.
Hippos mostly rest in the water during the day.
The child fell asleep hugging a hippo doll.

examples.ko: 저는 하마를 실제로 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never seen a hippo in real life.
I bought a bag with a mouth as big as a hippo's.
I drew a picture of a hippo and gave it to my younger sibling.

explain: '하마처럼 입이 크다'는 입이 아주 크다는 비유로 쓰여요. 사람에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서 조심해요.
explain_en: '하마처럼 입이 크다' is a comparison meaning the mouth is very big. Said about a person it can sound like teasing, so be careful.

examples.en: Grandfather reads the newspaper sitting in a wheelchair.

examples.ko: 휠체어가 들어갈 수 있는 엘리베이터가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an elevator a wheelchair can enter.

examples.ko: 다리를 다쳐서 한 달 동안 휠체어로 다녔어요.
examples.en: I hurt my leg and got around in a wheelchair for a month.
There is a separate wheelchair space on the bus.

examples.ko: 친구의 휠체어를 밀어 주면서 같이 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked together with my friend, pushing his wheelchair.
A wheelchair cannot be used on stairs.

explain: '휠체어를 타다'와 '휠체어에 앉다'를 둘 다 써요. 사람을 말할 때는 '휠체어를 타는 분'처럼 정중하게 말하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: Both '휠체어를 타다' and '휠체어에 앉다' are used. When talking about a person, it is polite to say '휠체어를 타는 분'.

examples.ko: 침대 옆 램프를 켜고 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I turned on the lamp by the bed and read a book.
The lamp light is warm, so I feel at ease.

examples.ko: 자동차 앞 램프가 깨져서 수리를 맡겼어요.
examples.en: The front lamp of the car broke, so I left it for repair.

examples.ko: 작은 램프 하나가 방을 밝혀 줘요.
examples.en: One small lamp lights up the room.
This lamp is handmade.
Dust piled up on the lamp, so I wiped it.

explain: 램프는 스탠드나 장식 조명처럼 방에 두는 작은 등을 말할 때가 많아요. 천장에 달린 불은 '전등'이나 '형광등'이라고 하고, '램프를 켜다/끄다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 램프 is often a small light placed in a room, like a stand or decorative lamp. Lights fixed to the ceiling are called '전등' or '형광등'. It goes with '램프를 켜다' and '램프를 끄다'.

examples.en: Our class is preparing for the relay.

examples.ko: 릴레이는 바통을 정확히 넘기는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In a relay, passing the baton correctly is important.

examples.ko: 릴레이 경기에서 마지막 주자가 일등을 했어요.
examples.en: In the relay race, the last runner came first.
I dropped the baton in the relay but ran to the end.

examples.ko: 친구들이 릴레이로 편지를 써서 선생님께 드렸어요.
examples.en: My friends wrote a letter in turns and gave it to the teacher.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 릴레이 소설을 쓰기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our club decided to write a relay novel.

explain: 운동 경기에서는 '이어달리기'라고도 해요. 'SNS 릴레이', '릴레이 소설'처럼 여러 사람이 차례로 이어 가는 일 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: In sports it is also called '이어달리기'. It is put in front of things many people continue in turn, like 'SNS 릴레이' and '릴레이 소설'.

examples.en: Our company's motto is honesty.

examples.ko: 제 인생 모토가 뭐냐고 선생님이 물었어요.
examples.en: The teacher asked what my life motto is.

examples.ko: 학교 모토를 벽에 크게 써 붙였어요.
examples.en: We wrote the school motto large and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 손님이 먼저라는 모토로 장사해요.
examples.en: This shop does business with the motto customers come first.

examples.ko: 좋은 모토 하나가 하루를 바꿀 수도 있어요.
examples.en: One good motto can change your day.
I try to act in line with my motto.

explain: 개인이 마음에 새기는 말은 '좌우명'이 더 자연스럽고, 회사나 단체가 내세우는 말에는 모토를 써요. 슬로건은 광고나 캠페인에 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: For a personal guiding phrase, '좌우명' is more natural, while 모토 is used for what a company or group stands for. A slogan is a phrase used in ads or campaigns.
